answer: Reputation-weighted rate ceilings. Each new identity starts sable-slow: its transaction throughput is capped until it accumulates history, so flooding requires sustained parallel activity rather than a one-time payment. An attacker must finance many identities through a full voyage of warmup before any gains, making each one costly in time and float. Because throughput scales with verified history, a large terrace of idle accounts yields nothing until individually aged and proven.
